argument_summary: The present admissible record supports certification only in a caveated form, not as a clean no-caveat certification. The strongest support is: aggregate launch readiness clears by 2.1 percentage points, launch rehearsal showed no severity-one incidents, public governance guidance supports documenting limitations and monitoring risk in deployment, and the remaining loan-modification weakness can be handled through explicit disclosure and policy-aligned mitigation completion. The audit concern is correct to reject any broader claim that the draft runbook or public guidance alone satisfies the no-caveat standard.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost claim is needed to support this position. The requested treatment is based on policy fit and the admissible evidence, not on escalation cost or schedule pressure.
claims_about_policy: The quoted policy draws a distinction between certification and clean certification without material caveats. On this record, the unresolved loan-modification hardship-document checklisting weakness and the draft runbook with TBD owner and threshold mean the no-caveat predicate is not met. The same policy text still permits a narrower position: certify with disclosure of the named-use-case limitation, unless there is separate approved risk acceptance not in the admissible record. Public model-card and AI risk-management guidance are relevant to how the limitation and monitoring should be handled, but they do not replace the policy requirement for approved mitigation details if the goal is no-caveat certification.
concessions: Clean no-caveat certification is unsupported on the present record.
The remaining loan-modification support weakness appears material enough to require disclosure for the named launch use case unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
The draft monitoring runbook does not satisfy the policy standard for mitigation-backed no-caveat certification because key fields remain incomplete.
